description: Issue #839 AC1, in the HERITAGE `to` spelling of the declaration slot. `spec/grammar.md` gives the grammar four declaration slots and `to` is one of them; `spec/conformance.md:150` makes Heritage "alternate spellings only. It does not add new semantics", so `to foo` twice must be exactly as illegal as `define foo` twice — same code, same params, same spans, differing only where the shorter keyword moves the column (`to` is three characters, so the name starts at column 4 rather than 8). This fixture exists because the corpus contained ZERO `to` declarations of any kind: measured, a mutant exempting `to` from the duplicate guard reproduced issue #839's ORIGINAL defect verbatim — this exact program printed `222` with no diagnostic while `check()` reported the collision — and passed all 886 fixtures, 3912 tests, examples and markdown. The corpus is the stack-neutral artifact another implementation must satisfy, so a `to`-slot rule pinned only in `packages/runtime` would not be portable. The two bodies print different values so the fixture discriminates between last-wins, first-wins and the ruling's rule.

diagnostics.message: you already defined foo on line 1.
